_comment: The environment values this stack owns in the scope's settings.json `env` block (the project's .claude/settings.json, or the account file for a global install). ONE source for the three guided commands: init's install phase asks the `ask: true` rows on its environment screen, configure step 9 shows and changes them, validate reconciles what is on disk against this list - a row absent from the file is a MISSING key the release introduced, a `renamed_from` still present is the old spelling, and a value failing `validate` is flagged with the expected shape. The installers seed every row ABSENT-ONLY on install and update (and apply the renames first, value carried over), so this catalog and the two installer twins must agree - `npm run lint` fails when they drift. Adding a variable: add the row here, seed it in both twins, and, when it replaces an older name, add the rename pair to migrations.json and give every consumer an old-name fallback. A row may carry `group_off`: it and every row naming it in `asked_with` are ONE feature, so the question that asks it also offers switching the feature off, which writes that value to the whole group (the walks never invent an off answer for a row without it). A row may also carry `secret: true`, and any key matching `secret_key_pattern` is treated the same way whether or not it has a row: its VALUE is never printed, never echoed back as a default, and never asked for through the chat - the walks report `set (N chars)` or `absent` and point the user at the file. Measured: seven credential exposures across one corpus, one of them an account settings.json read whole as a session's first tool call. A row may carry `former_defaults`: the values the stack seeded before its current `default`, read as the stack's own seed wherever a key's owner is judged without a ledger - never re-seeded, and never rewritten silently (the docs root's old default is moved only on an answer, `/alfred-code:update`). A row may carry `written: true`: it mirrors a choice the run just made rather than seeding a default, so a hand-edit is overwritten by the next install or update. No row carries it since the memory server left the stack (2026-10-24), and the run removes the old ALFRED_CODE_MEMORY_DB key. A change to ANY of these takes effect on the NEXT TOOL CALL - every hook reads its value per invocation - so no session restart is ever needed. State that when reporting a flip: a run once told the user to restart, and `grep -rn restart` over stack/, meta/, scripts/ and setup-plugin/ found no such claim anywhere, so the model had invented it (the instrumentation ledger's first row in fact landed 27.2 s later in the same session, covering 63 of 65 calls). A fact about the stack's own behaviour that the stack does not state gets invented.

env.what: the ONE folder, relative to the project, where Alfred Code keeps this project's data: the docs (`<root>/docs`), the hooks' machine state (`<root>/state`, the seats' handoff notes among it), the ledgers (`<root>/statistics`) and the sensitive-data store (`<root>/.sensitive-data`). Default `.alfred` at the project root - outside `.claude/`, where Claude Code prompts for every write. Its own `.gitignore` keeps everything but the docs out of git. Changing it (configure) MOVES the data inline: the docs and the sensitive-data store. No space, no `..`, never under `.claude/`.

how every capture's docs are VERSIONED - decided here, never guessed from git. `git`: the docs are committed and git versions them per branch, so a section is written into the doc file itself and nothing is ever written under `<docs-path>/.branches/` (promote and prune then have nothing to do). `local`: the machine-local overlay - a feature branch's sections live under `<docs-path>/.branches/<branch>/`, are merged into the mainline text at read time, and are folded into mainline when the branch merges. This decides HOW, never WHERE: the root stays ALFRED_CODE_DOCS_PATH. When the key is missing, the installers write `local` only if the docs are kept out of git - git ignores the docs root, or docs exist and none of them is committed - and `git` in every other case, a brand-new project included. `--docs-versioning git|local` (`-DocsVersioning` on Windows) writes a chosen value over the existing one; without it, an existing value is never touched. From then on the setting wins even where the repo disagrees, and `docs.js status` plus the session-start block report the disagreement rather than resolving it the other way.

the tool-usage instrumentation switch. `0` costs a node start per call that exits at the switch check and records nothing; `1` logs every tool call as one JSONL row for a measured run, then goes back to `0`. Flipping it takes effect on the next tool call; no session restart is needed.

guard-answer.js: a correction turn (a short prompt that follows an answer and carries a correction marker - 'no, ...', 'I meant', 'why did you', 'shorter') writes one `mode: probe` / `kind: correction` row to the hook-blocks ledger. `log` writes the row and injects nothing (the count-first week); `inject` also hands back the line 'this reads as a correction - keep what it teaches before continuing', naming the preferences docs for a preference and Claude Code's own memory for a lesson or project fact; `0` (or `off`, which the hook reads the same) is off.

check-turn-build.js: at Stop, ONE scoped build check per root for the source files the turn wrote - `tsc --noEmit -p` (the project's own tsc) for TypeScript, `dotnet build --no-restore -v q` for C# - the first 20 error lines handed back as a block, once per turn. `0` (the seed) is off; `1` turns it on, per project, after a measured week.

history-session.js: at Stop, a machine-local record of the session under `<data root>/state/history/` (its commits, the files left dirty, the user's AskUserQuestion answers - credential shapes scrubbed); at SessionStart, the last records of the same branch injected - this value is HOW MANY: `3` (the seed) up to `10`, a larger number read as 10, the block capped at 150 chars plus 150 per session. `0` is off (nothing recorded, nothing injected).

the per-message context, in TOKENS, at which a session on a 1M window is offered a fresh session instead of carrying on (an orchestration run is gated, a finished turn is offered). This row OWNS the whole gate: the rows riding with it are the 300K and 200K windows and the DEFAULT, and `group_off` means the question also offers turning the feature off, which writes `0` to all four. The window is the session model's own capacity (its row in the shipped `model-windows.json`) and takes the largest tier it reaches (1M and up, 300K and up, 200K and up); a window under 200K or unknown, or a tier left unset or garbage, takes ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_DEFAULT instead. The 400,000 default sits ABOVE the harness's own auto-compaction (measured preTokens 387,619-397,171), so on this window the turn-end offer is usually unreachable and the SessionStart compact route is what reaches you - lower it (250000, 350000) to be asked before the harness decides. To stop every fresh-session offer, set ALFRED_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT=1 rather than a tier to 0.

the same trigger in TOKENS for a window of 300K up to 1M. A model the shipped `model-windows.json` does not list has no known window, so it takes ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_DEFAULT, never this tier. `0` turns that tier off.

the same trigger in TOKENS for a window of 200K up to 300K (a 200K model). A window below the trigger holds it at 90% of the window. `0` turns that tier off. Each window size reads only its own variable.

the fresh-session TRIGGER, in tokens, for a session whose window has no tier: a model the `model-windows.json` shipped beside the hooks (the plugin's own on the plugin route) does not list, one whose window is under 200K, a session whose model is not known yet, or a tier variable left unset or garbage. The window is the model's own capacity from that table and nothing else - no id suffix, carry or settings alias is read - and this value is never a window and never an auto-compact window. The 180,000 seed fires before compaction in every window of 200K or more; until 2026-10-21 this key was the WINDOW an unlisted model was assumed to run in (seed 300,000), and an update moves that old seed to 180,000. Unset or garbage reads as 180,000; `0` turns the offer off for such a session.

what a long session does at the fresh-session trigger above. `0` (the seed) offers a fresh session there: an ask hands the work to a new session with a paste-ready resume, and Claude Code compacts at its own point. `1` compacts instead: the installer sets each model's `autoCompactWindow` in this project's settings to its trigger, no fresh-session ask is ever made, and the work goes on from the summary - read at session start, so it applies from the next session. Asked with the triggers; init's install phase passes the answer as `--auto-compact on|off`.

which memory this project uses. `default` (the seed) is Claude Code's own memory at its default place. `custom` switches Claude's own memory off (the installer writes a ledgered `autoMemoryEnabled: false` into this project's own settings file) and the memory tool TOOLS-PREFERENCES.md ranks holds the lessons. Asked in init's bootstrap and configure's Environment area, passed as `--memory default|custom`; read at session start, so it applies from the next session.

guard-fresh-session-start.js: the idle-gap offer. The prompt that ends a gap of this many HOURS since the last reply (or since an answered AskUserQuestion that waited that long) is offered a fresh session once per gap, with the carry and cold floor, when a resume recovers enough - a next-day resume ran 14 messages at 289.9k tokens unoffered before it (audit 2026-10-10 C09). Decimals work (`0.5`); `0` turns the idle offer off. Catalogued by the env audit of 2026-10-21: the hook read it before, but nothing listed it.

forge-session.js's ref watch: `all` (the seed) reports every branch and tag that moved with no gated act behind it - the default branch, the upstream, a branch the git preferences name, a commit from this checkout and any tag loud, the rest as one summary line; `loud-only` drops the summary line for a busy team repo, and the session's Forge: line says so, since the watch then no longer covers every branch; `publish-only` checks the remote only after a turn that made a forge call or a gated push, for a git login that asks every time (a security key that needs a touch, an approval dialog) - a move is then reported at the next such check, not the turn it happened. `forge-session:watch` in ALFRED_CODE_HOOKS_OFF turns the watch off.

a csv of hook names this project switches off, e.g. `guard-answer,instrument-tool-usage`. It is where the guided walk's hooks LAYER lands: every hook now arrives together inside the core alfred-code plugin, so there is no file to leave out of an install, and the rows an init or configure run does NOT pick are written here (that answer overwrites this value; every other run seeds it only when absent). Matching is exact on the base name, `.js` optional; a prefix never matches. A hook's PART is switched off the same way, as `<hook>:<part>`: `docs-session:block` (the session-start orientation), `docs-session:gate` (the first-change hold), `docs-session:ask` (the end-of-session doc ask), `guard-ungated-commit:push` (the publish half of the commit gate), `guard-stop-contract:rotate` (the credential rotate ask), `guard-stop-contract:done` (the done-gate probe) and `guard-fresh-session-start:builtin-review` (the deny of the model's call to Claude Code's bundled /code-review and /security-review, 2026-10-22) - each but the last was its own `=0` key before the env audit of 2026-10-21, and an update folds a stored `0` in here.
